font.b: What is the claim?

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 311px; height: 1px; padding-top: 200px; margin-left: 202px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 63px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b:
The Bible possesses a textual and historical preservation that is superior to all alternatives, which are not authorized by God
(ie. deceptive or demonic in origin).

div.font: Specifically: if the resurrection of Jesus is shown to be decisively true (without any reasonable alternative), then it incapacitates any argument that Jesus was not divine.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 311px; height: 1px; padding-top: 200px; margin-left: 517px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 63px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b:
The Quran possesses a preservation and inimitability that is superior to all alternatives, which are not authorized by God
(ie. deceptive or demonic in origin).

div.font: Specifically: if the Quran is shown to be perfectly preserved and cannot have been produced by a human being, then it incapacitates any argument that Jesus was divine.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 178px; height: 1px; padding-top: 293px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 61px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: Is it ontologically possible and epistemologically attainable?

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 311px; height: 1px; padding-top: 265px; margin-left: 202px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 63px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Yes

div.font: Texts and historical events can be preserved over time, and their preservation can be analyzed by eliminating alternatives for fabrication and falsehood .

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 311px; height: 1px; padding-top: 265px; margin-left: 517px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 63px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Yes

div.font: Texts and historical events can be preserved over time, and their preservation can be analyzed by eliminating alternatives for fabrication and falsehood

span.style: font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.font: Additionally, humans have a hard limit to what they are capable of doing, so anything that falls beyond that limit would verify inimitability.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 178px; height: 1px; padding-top: 383px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 111px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b:
What are the criteria for success
and failure?

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 311px; height: 1px; padding-top: 330px; margin-left: 202px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 113px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Truth is defined/identified by consistency and reality, and falsehood by inconsistency and contradiction with reality.

div.font: If the Bible is authorized by God, then it must be the epitome of consistency and correspondence with reality. As a result, if all falsehoods necessarily contradict with reality, then the Quran cannot possess the same level of consistency and coherence as the Bible.

Therefore, success is showing that the Bible has a better form of preservation than the Quran and is more consistent and coherent. Failure is if the Quran's preservation and inimitability are stronger than the Bible's, since no manmade effort can ever surpass God's power.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 311px; height: 1px; padding-top: 330px; margin-left: 517px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 113px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Truth is defined/identified by consistency and reality, and falsehood by inconsistency and contradiction with reality.

div.font: If the Quran is authorized by God, then it must be the epitome of consistency and correspondence with reality. As a result, if all falsehoods necessarily contradict with reality, then the Bible cannot possess the same level of consistency and coherence as the Quran.

Therefore, success is showing that the Quran is truly inimitable, has a better form of preservation than the Bible, and is more consistent and coherent. Failure is if the Quran could have been manmade, or if Bible's preservation and historical reliability are stronger than the Quran's - since no manmade effort can ever surpass God's power.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 808px; height: 1px; padding-top: 173px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 18px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 178px; height: 1px; padding-top: 538px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 71px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Who were the eyewitnesses, and what did they bear witness to?

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 311px; height: 1px; padding-top: 505px; margin-left: 202px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 73px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Three significant events: Jesus' 3-year earthly ministry, 40 days of Jesus' resurrection, and the post-resurrection vision that appeared to Paul

div.font: Thousands of people witnessed Jesus's ministry (about 3 years long), while over 500 witnessed his 40-day bodily resurrection (between 30-33 AD). Finally, Paul witnessed a spiritual and personal vision of Jesus (between 33-36 AD).

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 311px; height: 1px; padding-top: 505px; margin-left: 517px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 73px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Two significant events: the Quran's revelation to the Prophet Muhammad over 23 years, and his character, personality, and ministry in that time period

div.font: Tens of thousands of people witnessed the Quran's revelation to the Prophet Muhammad (which were unique, context-specific events that occurred from 610-632 AD), and even more witnessed his ministry in that time.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 178px; height: 1px; padding-top: 678px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 201px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b:
How reliable was the cultural
context for preserving oral tradition accurately?

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 311px; height: 1px; padding-top: 580px; margin-left: 202px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 203px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Jewish oral tradition preserved core concepts, without verbatim transmission

div.span: The Jewish culture at the time had a strong tradition of oral preservation - and their preserved texts meant that verbatim oral transmission was unnecessary.

The Bible largely reflects this: at least 35-80 years had passed after Jesus' ministry before the Gospels were written, in which cultural and linguistic barriers were crossed (transitioning from Jewish and Aramaic to Greek and Roman). Given the oral tradition before the texts were written and their standardization in a foreign language, this supports the claim that core concepts were preserved.

div.font: T

span.style: font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: his makes verbatim preservation unlikely, but this is in line with classical views, as the tradition is seen as "living" where the core is preserved without significant corruption.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 311px; height: 1px; padding-top: 580px; margin-left: 517px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 203px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Verbatim preservation with the Quran, semi-verbatim preservation with the Prophet's life and character

div.font: The 7th century Arabian culture already had an exceptionally strong tradition of oral preservation, as they lacked any written and textual presence before the Quran - which was the first completed written work of

span.style: font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));
font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));
font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: literature ever written. This meant that their oral literature before (and during) the Quran's revelation relied heavily on verbatim memorization in order to be preserved.

div.font: The Quran largely reflects this: it was memorized verbatim by all witnesses, with daily, audible, and communal prayers serving as a living verification by the community, in a language that continues to exist today and is geographically widespread. It was also preserved only in the Arabic that it was revealed in - with its rasm (consonantal skeleton) serving as its preservation in written form (and all translations only being considered as exegeses of the Arabic recitation) - thus eliminating possibilities of mythologization and gradual shifts in translation.

div.span: As for the Prophet's life and character, its oral tradition lasted for 100-200 years before being written and codified. As such, what is recorded isn't necessarily a verbatim transmission of what the original narrators said (with more room for fabrication and error) - the core narrative being reliably preserved, but requiring specialized scholarly effort to authenticate.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 178px; height: 1px; padding-top: 865px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 166px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: When was the text written and standardized, and by whom?

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 311px; height: 1px; padding-top: 785px; margin-left: 202px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 168px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Written by multiple authors (not Jesus) sometime 10-70 years after Jesus' ministry, while the canon was standardized in 382 AD by the Council of Rome

div.font: The earliest New Testament texts were written 7-12 years after Jesus' ministry (in the earliest estimates), and were likely Galatians, Thessalonians (both by Paul), and possibly even James (although this is not a majority view). However (excluding James), Paul was not a witness to Jesus' earthly ministry nor his resurrection - and since the Gospels

span.style: font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));
font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));
font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: were written 10-70 years after Jesus (considering both early and late dating), this puts them being written at a later time than the non-eyewitness accounts. This also means that none of the texts are authored by Jesus himself.

Meanwhile, heresies were prevalent from Paul's ministry and continued into 400 AD, with many heretical/apocryphal works being written. This resulted in a gradual process of standardization that culminated in the Council of Rome in 382 AD, establishing the New Testament canon (which was first proposed by Irenaeus in 180 AD).

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 311px; height: 1px; padding-top: 785px; margin-left: 517px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 168px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Three significant events:

the writing and ordering of the Quran during the Prophet Muhammad's life, the first complete written Quran being codified 2 years after his death, and the written standardization of the dialect/accent 20 years after his death

div.font: While the Quran was primarily memorized verbatim by the community, it was also written by the Prophet's scribes - namely, Zaid b. Thabit and his team - shortly after the revelation occurred. After his death, Abu Bakr (the first caliph after the Prophet) compiled the first written text of the entire Quran, as it was textually fragmented so far (because the Quran was revealed in context-specific situations). Finally, as Islam began to spread to the non-Arabian world, the dialect and diacritics were standardized 20 years after the Prophet's death by the fourth caliph, Uthman.

div.span: As for the Prophet's life and character, this started to be written down within 100 years after the Prophet's death, with the most rigorous works (the 6 Sahih Collections) were written 200 years after his death (or 300-500 years for the Shia collections).

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 178px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1018px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 131px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: What corroborating archaeological finds are there?

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 311px; height: 1px; padding-top: 955px; margin-left: 202px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 133px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Strong historical and cultural corroboration, with earliest manuscripts of the New Testament dating to 125 AD

div.font: Some non-Christian writers (namely, Josephus and Tacitus, around 100 AD) reference Jesus in their historical works - although, none of them mention his resurrection or divinity

span.style: font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));
font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: . Moreover, the locations of cities, cultural practices of the Jews and Romans, and inscriptions of historical people all corroborate what is mentioned in the New Testament. Meanwhile, the earliest manuscript we have dates to 125 AD, although that is the exception: the vast majority of them are between 300-400 AD.

div.font: Therefore, as each of the New Testament books are claimed to have been written long before 125 AD, the primary means of dating when they were written is a purely logical endeavor, without corroborating archaeological manuscripts to verify.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 311px; height: 1px; padding-top: 955px; margin-left: 517px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 133px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Overwhelming historical and cultural corroboration, with the earliest manuscripts dating to the Prophet's life

div.font: The Islamic Golden Age was a direct result of the Prophet's legacy, leaving us with overwhelming evidence of Islam's influence. Moreover, every single geographical location relevant to the Prophet's life is well known and corroborated, as well as extensive knowledge into the Prophet's life and the practices of the early Muslims. Finally, the earliest Quranic manuscript we have dates to the Prophet's own lifetime (which is verbatim of what we have now), although the vast majority of them are between 100-200 years after the Prophet's death.
Therefore, not only is the Quran reliably preserved verbatim by communal memorization, it is also soundly verifiable through archaeological means.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 808px; height: 1px; padding-top: 478px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 18px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 808px; height: 1px; padding-top: 108px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.font: Note that the following sections only compare trinitarianism (sourced by the New Testament) and monotheism (sourced by the Quran). Even though Atheism's rebuttals fit the natural data, it neither explains why reality exists, nor does it actually refute (or reduce confidence in) the alignment of a transcendent creator with reality. And Polytheism is set aside becuase a plurality of ultimate powers doesn’t naturally yield the unified, law-governed order we actually observe - and multiplying ultimate agents introduces unexplained conflict/coordination that the world’s tight regularities don’t display.
